Compare medfit's Product-Null LR with OpenMx or lavaan

Source: R/compare-lr.R
compare_lr.Rd

Bounded FIML fits are refused before an external-engine comparison or refit; this function does not extend their supported inference. See fit_sem().

Runs the likelihood-ratio test of a product null (\(a b = 0\)) in an external SEM engine and compares it with medfit's own mbco_sem() statistic. A general-purpose optimizer handed the nonlinear constraint \(a b = 0\) can drop it (OpenMx at a zero start) or stop at the wrong branch (lavaan), which reports a statistic above the true minimum. compare_lr() flags exactly those cases and nothing else.

A warning is raised only on observed evidence, never because an LR is zero: medfit_warning_engine_constraint_dropped when the engine's returned fit violates the product constraint, and medfit_warning_engine_statistic_above_max when the engine's statistic exceeds medfit's. Both inherit from medfit_warning_engine_comparison. If medfit has no accepted reference, the engines' unrestricted fits differ from medfit's, or a run fails or cannot be checked, the verdict is "unresolved" and neither side is blamed. medfit has no accepted reference when one of its own refits cannot be fitted (see mbco_sem()): the reference LR is then NA and the result is a comparison with that verdict, not an error.

Only observed-variable models are compared. With either engine, a saturated mean structure (every intercept free) and fixed_x (all, a named subset or a lenient subset) are supported: the fixed exogenous moments are written to the engine as fixed parameters at their sample values (in OpenMx, a fit with a mean structure is run on the raw data the fit used). Latent variables, product terms, fixed or constrained intercepts, weights, factors, other fixed or shared parameters, start/bound modifiers and constraints in the model are refused by name.

Known limit (#320): the flip of the fit_sem() defaults in 0.15.0 does not change what the comparison finds. On the pinned design (15 seeds by 4 cells, 60 runs per engine), the lavaan run ends above medfit's reference in 18 of 60 runs and the OpenMx run in 13 of 60, the same counts as under the 0.14.x defaults. Each is reported as medfit_warning_engine_statistic_above_max, and no row is mislabeled.

Usage

compare_lr(object, paths, engine = c("lavaan", "openmx"), tolerance = 1e-04)

Arguments

object

A SEMFit from fit_sem().

paths

Character vector: the labels of the regression paths whose product is the indirect effect, as in mbco_sem().

engine

"lavaan" or "openmx". The package must be installed.

tolerance

Relative tolerance on the LR difference, scaled by max(1, LR). Default 1e-4; values above 1e-2 are refused, because a loose tolerance would call different statistics equal.

Value

An object of class medfit_lr_comparison: a list with verdict ("agree", "disagree" or "unresolved"), reason, reference (medfit's LR, NA when it has none, and whether it was accepted), runs (one row per engine start with the LR, convergence, constraint residual and status) and engine.

See also

mbco_sem(), fit_sem()

Examples

# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("lavaan", quietly = TRUE)) {
  fit <- fit_sem(
    "mediator1 ~ a*treatment\noutcome ~ b*mediator1 + cp*treatment",
    data = mediation_demo, fixed_x = FALSE, meanstructure = NULL
  )
  compare_lr(fit, paths = c("a", "b"), engine = "lavaan")
}
#> medfit LR comparison (lavaan, a*b = 0): agree
#>   medfit reference LR 17.5574 (accepted)
#>  engine version   start      lr converged     residual status
#>  lavaan   0.7.3 default 17.5574      TRUE 2.418474e-09  agree
#>  lavaan   0.7.3    zero 17.5574      TRUE 3.773233e-09  agree
# }
